Ivy H.: Heads-up — onboarding found a subtle parity + dim issue with embeddings+rerank when batching helper + retries are involved. Node sample lost an item and one returned vector had 768 dims while others were 1024, causing the reranker to drop it.

Rafael M.: thanks. short repro? sounds like combined issues: positional stitch + model-fallback dim change.

Ivy H.: repro (sanitized): send 6 inputs with batch_helper.max_batch_size=4. Sequence: sub-batch1 -> 200 (4 items), sub-batch2 -> 401 auth refresh -> client retries -> server responds 200 but one item uses quantized fallback (768 dim). Node final array had 5 embeddings (one missing) and one 768-d vector; python returned 6 items and included per-item ids and dims.

Jun P.: node helper still uses position-based concat unless tag_ids is enabled, right? that explains missing item when retry replay returned a trimmed array.

Mira O.: correct. python attaches per-item uuids by default. Node opted for byte savings. We debated compact ids (4-8 bytes) but worried about collisions in high-concurrency tenants.

Rafael M.: collision risk is low if we namespace by request_ts + small seq. But add a short checksum or include per-item model_id/dim in response object to be safe. Server should never mix dims silently in a single response.

Ivy H.: for the customer, I enabled batch_helper.tag_ids=true and set header X-Response-Shape: object_items so server returned [{embedding,input,client_id,model_id,dim}]. That fixed mapping and reranker kept the 768 item (it logs a warning instead of dropping).

Jun P.: action items: 1) change node helper to auto-enable tag_ids when retry/backoff configured; 2) server: reject mixed-dim responses or normalize dims, and add meta.dedupe_count + meta.sub_batch_ids; 3) add opt-in header X-Response-Shape: object_items; 4) add docs quicknote about auth-refresh causing replay.

ops-bot: Created DEVEX-5399: "node: auto-enable compact ids on retry; server normalize dims or include per-item meta; add dedupe_count & object_items opt-in"  https://rwd.in/DEVEX-5399

Mira O.: one more nuance: if we introduce compact_id we should also provide a debug mode that emits full uuids for customers who want absolute tracing during onboarding. low-overhead default compact ids + debug full ids should cover both perf and observability.

Ivy H.: agreed. i'll paste a tiny node/python repro + raw http trace into DEVEX-5399 and follow up with the customer. thanks! :thumbsup:
